skill2: ■ Activates after landing 60 normal attacks. Affects the 2 ally unit(s) with the lowest HP percentage.
■ Activates after landing 120 normal attacks. Affects the 2 ally unit(s) with the lowest HP percentage.

caveats: ⚑ Her only offensive channel is the S1 boss debuff (Damage Taken ▲17.18%/5s on a 120-hit counter). Every number below the banner that is not literally in the kit text is an unmeasured estimate.

⚑ The 120/60 thresholds count LANDED normal attacks in the kit's wording; the engine's hitCount trigger counts rounds the owner fires. With SMG accuracy below 100% the real threshold arrives later than the sim's, so both S1 uptime and the (unmodeled) S2 windows are optimistic.

⚑ Debuff uptime is cadence-bound, not kit-bound: 120 rounds is exactly one magazine (ammo 120, reloadFrames 81), so S1 fires roughly once per magazine cycle and its 5-second window covers only a fraction of that cycle. The duty cycle moves with the datamined SMG cadence, which is a known-unreliable field.

S2's two ally lines carry no offensive channel in the schema: 'Incoming healing ▲' has no StatKey, and ally-side 'Damage Taken ▼' is not expressible (damageTakenPct is the boss-side debuff, positive = boss takes more). They are recorded verbatim in unmodeled rather than approximated.

The burst heal models the recovery EVENT stream only (10 ticks at 1 s) — no HP pool exists at scope lock, so the 10.03%-of-caster-Max-HP magnitude is not represented. The ticks matter because they fire teammates' 'recovery' triggers.
alliesLowestHp resolves to the leftmost 2 allies in v1 (no HP pool, immortal boss) — a documented engine stand-in, not a kit reading.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Sakura Suzuhara is an SMG/Water/Supporter Burst I with no damage lines of her own. Modeled today: S1's recurring 120-round boss debuff (Damage Taken ▲17.18% for 5 s, target enemy) and the burst's 10-tick recovery stream to the 2 lowest-HP allies (burstCast trigger, event-only — no HP amount). Deliberately unmodeled: both S2 ally lines (incoming-healing lift and ally damage-taken reduction), neither of which has a schema channel and neither of which moves damage at scope lock. Trigger identity is read literally: both S1 and S2 activation clauses are hit-count, and the burst block has no activation clause of its own, so it is keyed to her own burst cast.

audit.effectOrReason: trigger hitCount{count:120} — recurring per-magazine counter, not a one-shot
target {kind:'enemy'} — boss-held debuff, benefits the whole team
trigger would be hitCount{count:60}, but its sole effect line has no schema channel — whole block unmodeled
no StatKey for incoming-healing amplification; heals are modeled as events with no HP amount, so the multiplier has nothing to scale
trigger would be hitCount{count:120}; its effect line has no schema channel
ally-side damage reduction; damageTakenPct is the enemy-side debuff channel (positive = boss takes more) — encoding -14.97 on allies would be a mis-scope, not a model. No boss damage at scope lock
target alliesLowestHp{count:2}, no excludeSelf (kit does not exclude the user)
heal{ticks:10,intervalSec:1} on burstCast — emits 10 recovery events that keep teammates' on-recovery consumers refreshed; the 10.03%-of-caster-Max-HP magnitude is unrepresentable (no HP pool)

flags.estimate: count 120 as authored, i.e. 120 rounds fired ≈ one full magazine
flags.reasoning: The kit says 'after landing 120 normal attacks'; the engine's hitCount counts ROUNDS the owner fires, not rounds that connect. SMG spread means landed < fired, so the real activation is later than the sim's and the debuff's duty cycle is over-credited. Her whole team contribution is this debuff's uptime, so the error is not marginal — it scales the entire value of the unit.
flags.recipe: Focus-record her in a graded comp and count the interval between consecutive Damage Taken ▲ applications on the boss (buff icon appearance, or the ▲ debuff aura). Compare against magazine boundaries read off the ammo counter: if the debuff lands exactly at the reload, fired-count is right; if it lags into the next magazine, raise count by the observed landing fraction.

flags.field: cadence tuple (pullsPerSec / effective SMG fire rate)
flags.estimate: engine default SMG cadence, unmodified by this override
flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑: the datamined rate_of_fire is nominal and the game fires on 60fps frame boundaries, so effective = 60/ceil(60/nominal). Both of this unit's live and unmodeled triggers are hit-count-keyed, which makes debuff uptime a direct function of cadence rather than of any kit value — a cadence error propagates 1:1 into the S1 debuff's duty cycle.
flags.recipe: Read shots/sec directly off the ammo counter in a focus recording (the instrument that measures the disputed quantity), not off full-burst counts, which are downstream of gauge. Cross-check the 120-round magazine drain time against reloadFrames 81.

flags.field: skill1[0].effects[0] uptime (duty cycle, not a kit value)
flags.estimate: ~5 s of Damage Taken ▲17.18% per ~(120 rounds + 81 frames reload) cycle
flags.reasoning: The 17.18% and the 5 s are both kit-literal, but the fraction of the fight the boss actually carries the debuff is derived entirely from cadence + the counting rule above, neither of which is measured. Any board comparison of this unit is really a comparison of that duty cycle.
flags.recipe: Count Damage Taken ▲ application timestamps over a 180 s scope-lock fight from a focus recording; uptime = 5 s × applications / 180. Score against the sim's buffApply event stream filtered to stat 'damageTakenPct', value 17.18.

flags.estimate: burstCast — fires only on rotations where she casts her own Burst I
flags.reasoning: The burst block carries no activation clause, so the slot's own default applies: a self burst-effect keyed to the owner's cast, not to team full-burst entry. Keying it to fullBurstEnter would over-fire whenever another Burst I chains the rotation. Low risk here (the effect is heal-only) but it matters to any teammate whose damage is gated on 'when recovery takes effect'.
flags.recipe: Any comp pairing her with an on-recovery consumer: check that the consumer's buff applications track her burst casts, not every full-burst entry.

flags.estimate: event-only: 10 recovery events, no HP amount
flags.reasoning: The engine models heals as recovery events (no HP pool at scope lock, immortal boss). The 10.03%-of-caster-final-Max-HP magnitude is therefore recorded in prose only. This is correct for damage purposes today but silently drops the value if a future consumer scales off healed AMOUNT rather than the recovery event.
flags.recipe: None needed while no consumer reads heal magnitude. Revisit if a kit lands that scales off amount healed; the kit value 10.03% × caster final Max HP × 10 ticks is already stated here.

flags.estimate: zero damage contribution at scope lock
flags.reasoning: Incoming-healing amplification has no StatKey and nothing to scale (heals carry no amount); ally damage-taken reduction has no ally-side channel and no incoming boss damage to reduce. Both are genuinely inert for this sim's purpose rather than convenient skips — but the skip is a scope claim, not a kit claim, and would become wrong if boss damage were ever modeled.
flags.recipe: Re-audit if an HP pool or boss damage lands. Until then the claim is verifiable by inspection: no StatKey exists for either line in types.ts.
